purpose: Define the strongest defensible path from retail units toward package-size-adjusted physical food quantity while preserving the current absence of a public 2026 national gram/calorie series.
authoritative_method_source: USDA Economic Research Service Food-at-Home Monthly Area Prices (F-MAP)

method.underlying_data: Circana retail scanner sales and quantity data
method.unit_value: weighted purchase dollars divided by weighted purchase grams, reported per 100 grams
package_weight_normalization: ounces -> grams using 28.35 grams per ounce
pounds -> grams using 28.35 x 16 grams per pound
fluid ounces -> grams using 29.57 grams per fluid ounce
method.coverage: 90 food-at-home groups across 15 U.S. geographic areas

critical_availability_limit.interpretation: USDA establishes that package-adjusted physical quantity can be measured in grams from scanner data, but the currently public F-MAP files do not provide a 2026 national gram series. Therefore no 2026 mass trend may be invented from the historical methodology.

known_windows: first half 2026 food/beverage dollars +2.2% while reported volume was flat and price/mix +2.3%
latest four weeks through 2026-07-12 reported volume -0.6% while price/mix +2.6%

interpretive_rules: Retail units are not identical to grams, calories, nutrition, or household food adequacy.
Reported scanner volume is stronger than dollar sales for quantity direction but must retain the vendor's definition unless package-level mass fields are directly custodied.
Shrinkflation can cause unit counts to overstate physical quantity if package size falls.
Product-mix changes can change calories, nutrition quality, or mass even when retail unit counts are stable.
Historical USDA methodology validates a future gram-normalized analysis method; it does not itself provide contemporary 2026 quantities.
No causal attribution from reduced physical acquisition to diesel or shipping may be made solely from temporal co-movement.
next_evidence_targets: contemporary package-level scanner data containing units and package weight
a 2026 USDA or other authoritative national gram/weight series if released
Purchase-to-Plate or nutrition-linked scanner outputs capable of mapping purchases to calories/nutrients
household-level acquisition data permitting income and essential-cost stratification
